message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p2 with $363 and the dark blue monopoly (PARK_PLACE and BOARDWALK). I have cash but no houses yet. Other players are much richer.

I can build one house on the dark blue for $200, leaving $163. I'm weighing whether that rent increase is worth the cash outlay.

One house would raise dark blue rent to $175 on Park Place and $200 on Boardwalk. The even-build rule means only one property gets the house while the other keeps its doubled base rent. Dark blues are late on the board, so landing probability is low.

One house would leave only $163, which is too thin. Three houses would cost $600 and likely bankrupt me. The other players' unimproved properties pose little threat.

I'm the only player with a monopoly, so rent is low and bankruptcy risk is minimal. I need cash to buy blocking properties like Connecticut, Virginia, and Reading RR. Building one house would leave me with only $163.

I can only afford Connecticut or Baltic with the remaining cash. The dark blue house would raise rent by about $100 on Boardwalk or $105 on Park Place. That is a large return, but landing there once is unlikely.

Standard strategy favors saving cash rather than building one house on the dark blue. Three houses on both properties would cost $1200, which is impossible with current funds. Mortgaging some holdings could raise the needed cash instead.

Mortgaging a property in the dark blue monopoly would destroy the rent boost and block future building. I can mortgage non-monopoly holdings for roughly $395, plus my $363 cash, giving me about $758 total. That covers three houses on both properties, leaving about $158, or two houses on one and one on the other.

Mortgaging properties does not transfer ownership, so blocking still works. The real win condition is the dark blue monopoly with houses, since no other player has a monopoly yet.

The rent curve confirms one house is too weak. Boardwalk jumps from $100 to $200 to $600, and Park Place from $70 to $175 to $500. Two houses on both properties cost $800 total, but mortgaging all non-monopoly holdings only yields $758. I am $42 short of that target.

The best even-build split is two houses on Boardwalk and one on Park Place. That costs $600 and leaves $158 cash. I would collect no rent from mortgaged properties, and the income tax of $200 is unaffordable.

I cannot mortgage the dark blue properties while they have houses. Selling three houses back at half price would raise about $300, enough to pay the income tax. I am reconsidering whether to build now or wait until after the orbit, since I just landed on Vermont Avenue and will soon reach Connecticut.

I mapped the board from Vermont Avenue. Connecticut ($120) is unowned and p3 wants it for a light blue monopoly. Virginia ($160) is also unowned and critical for blocking p1's pink set. St. Charles, States, and Tennessee are already owned by other players.

I am on Vermont Avenue. The next roll will likely land me on Connecticut, Virginia, or an unowned yellow. I am counting the exact board positions to confirm.

I mapped the full board from Vermont Avenue. A roll of 2 lands on unowned Connecticut ($120), which I must buy to block p3. A roll of 5 hits Electric Company, where p4 owns it and I own Water Works.

Roll 7 is the most likely landing spot, hitting unowned Virginia ($160). Connecticut is only reachable on a roll of 2. St James is another unowned target at roll 9. With $363 cash, I can buy any of these properties directly without mortgaging.

I should not build a house yet. Keeping cash is safer for the upcoming orbit. I also considered trading, but selling Kentucky to p3 would let them complete a red monopoly. That would be very dangerous.

I rejected trading away St. Charles to p1, since that would let them complete the pink monopoly while Virginia remains unowned. I also refused to trade Vermont to p3 for the same reason; two light blues are too dangerous to let them build. I noted that p4 owns Electric Company and I own Water Works.

Selling Water Works would let p4 complete a utility monopoly, but that is not worth the cash. I have Penn RR and p1 has B&O, so I cannot buy a railroad set. p3 will not sell both red properties to me; they want Kentucky in return. p1 might sell States if I overpay, since Virginia remains unowned.

I had the standard Monopoly colors wrong. St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue are orange, not red. I am rechecking the color map to verify the correct sets.

I have mapped the full color sets. Light blues are Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut. Pinks are St. Charles, States, and Virginia. Oranges are St. James, Tennessee, and New York. Reds are Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. Yellows are Atlantic, Ventnor, and Marvin Gardens. Greens are Pacific, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania. Dark blues are Park Place and Boardwalk.

P3 owns Oriental, Tennessee, and Illinois. P1 owns States, Indiana, B&O, and Pennsylvania. P4 owns Mediterranean, Electric Company, New York, and North Carolina. I own Vermont, St. Charles, Penn RR, Kentucky, Water Works, Park Place, and Boardwalk.

No player currently holds two of three properties in any color set. The reds are split across three players, the oranges are split, the pinks are split, and the light blues are split. Only the dark blue set is fully owned by me.

Baltic would complete p4's brown set, and Pacific would let p1 or p4 finish their green set. St James and the yellows are also unowned and could be picked up as footholds. Connecticut is unowned, so it cannot be traded for.

I considered trading for a second monopoly, but no player will sell the pieces I need at a price that works. Completing the red set would require two trades and is unlikely to succeed. Acquiring the orange set would also need two trades and still leave St James unowned.

Building now is premature. One house on dark blue would barely affect the game. Mortgaging everything to build two houses would leave me unable to buy Connecticut, Virginia, or St James. Those properties block opponents from completing color sets. If p3 acquires Connecticut, they would own two light blues and pressure me for Vermont. Light blue houses cost only fifty dollars, so they could build quickly. I should not let p3 get Connecticut if I can buy it.

Building one house leaves about $163. That covers Connecticut or Virginia now, but St James at $180 is impossible if I build. Virginia costs $160 and requires no rent payment. The most likely landing spots are roll 7 for Virginia and roll 6 for States rent.

A trade with p3 for Illinois would not complete a color set. They would still need Connecticut, and they might buy it to pressure me for Vermont. I will end my turn without building.

I rejected trading Kentucky for Illinois because neither player would complete a color set. A trade with p1 for Indiana would give them two pink properties and leave the red set incomplete, since p3 still holds Illinois. I am now considering buying Indiana from p1 and Illinois from p3 over two turns to build a second red monopoly while keeping dark blue.

I cannot afford Indiana and Illinois in one trade. I am now considering selling Water Works to p4 for about three hundred dollars. That would give me roughly seven hundred dollars, enough to build three houses on dark blue and leave about one hundred dollars.

A rejected trade proposal wastes the action, and it is unclear whether I can act again afterward. Selling Water Works for four hundred dollars would leave more cash than selling for three hundred.

P4 is conservative and has already rejected a high offer for New York. They are unlikely to accept Water Works for a premium. A trade now offers no clear value. Mortgaging is unnecessary.

Mortgaging would cost ten percent to reverse. One house on dark blue yields only about eight dollars in expected rent per round, so the payback period is roughly twenty-five rounds.

The house is only a net cost of about one hundred dollars, since half the purchase price can be recovered. The cash is more valuable than the house, however, because it can buy St James, Virginia, Connecticut, and Reading to block opponents and provide a safety buffer. I will keep the cash and reassess after the orbit.
